title: AkcliSymbolPins
description: Input document for `akcli library new-symbol`: a declarative pin table that akcli lays out into a .kicad_sym. Coordinates are NEVER authored here — the generator computes them, because coordinate layout is exactly where hand-written symbols acquire two pins on one point (which KiCad joins into one node, with no ERC violation). Both `side` and `type` are REQUIRED per pin and are never guessed: a symbol whose electrical types were left unset turns KiCad's ERC pin-conflict matrix into a rubber stamp. The loader in src/akcli/symbol_spec.py is the executable copy of this contract; tests/test_symbol_pins_schema.py asserts the two agree.

protocol_version.description: Bumped only on a breaking change to this document shape.

name.description: Symbol name; also the Value property. KiCad's {token} escaping is applied on write, so a literal '/' or ':' is fine here.

reference_prefix.description: Reference designator prefix (the Reference property), e.g. 'U', 'J', 'RN'.

pins.description: The pin table, in the order it should read. Pin numbers must be unique. A symbol with no pins connects nothing and is refused.

number.description: Package pad identifier, e.g. '1' or 'A12'. Unique within the symbol.

name.description: Pin function name. Use "" for an unnamed pin (emitted as KiCad's '~').

type.description: KiCad electrical-type grammar token, emitted verbatim. REQUIRED — never defaulted. 'free'/'unspecified' are accepted but flagged by SYMLIB_PIN_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED.

side.description: Which body edge the pin attaches to. REQUIRED — the generator never infers a side from a pin name.

group.description: Optional functional grouping. Within one side, pins are ordered by their group's FIRST APPEARANCE in this array, then by array order — so related pins stay together and the layout is stable.

hidden.description: Emit the pin with `(hide yes)`. Usual case: the redundant members of a stacked power-pin group.

stack_with.description: Number of the pin whose coordinate this pin shares — the ONLY sanctioned same-coordinate case. The target must be on the same side, must not itself be stacked, and must carry the SAME name and the SAME type (KiCad's stacked-pin convention). Anything else on one point is an electrical mis-join and is refused.

body.description: Optional geometry overrides. Omit it and the body is sized from the pin counts and name lengths.

width_mil.description: Widen the body to at least this many mils (rounded up to a 200-mil multiple so pins stay on the 100-mil grid). It can only WIDEN: shrinking below the computed minimum would push top/bottom pins onto the left/right pin columns.
